response.sql:
WITH item_town AS (
    SELECT
        oi.order_item_id,
        c.town_city,
        AVG(ili.product_price) AS item_avg_price,
        AVG(ili.derived_product_cost / NULLIF(ili.derived_total_cost, 0)) AS item_avg_ratio
    FROM Invoice_Line_Items AS ili
    JOIN Order_Items AS oi ON oi.order_item_id = ili.order_item_id
    JOIN Orders AS o ON o.order_id = oi.order_id
    JOIN Customers AS c ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id
    GROUP BY oi.order_item_id, c.town_city
), town_averages AS (
    SELECT
        town_city,
        AVG(item_avg_price) AS average_price,
        AVG(item_avg_ratio) AS average_ratio
    FROM item_town
    GROUP BY town_city
), cross_town AS (
    SELECT AVG(average_ratio) AS cross_town_average_ratio
    FROM town_averages
)
SELECT
    t.town_city AS town,
    t.average_price,
    t.average_ratio,
    t.average_ratio - x.cross_town_average_ratio AS amount_above_cross_town_average
FROM town_averages AS t
CROSS JOIN cross_town AS x
WHERE t.average_ratio > x.cross_town_average_ratio;

assumptions.assumption: The two-stage averages are unweighted: average available invoice-line values per order item and town, then give each resulting order item equal weight in that town's average. Null values are ignored at each AVG; a zero total cost yields a missing ratio.
